change.title: Azure AD Graph API (graph.windows.net) fully retired after extended access ended; migrate to Microsoft Graph

source.quote: August 31, 2025: End of extended access to Azure AD Graph. Azure AD Graph will be fully retired.

tasks.reasoning:
The repo calls Azure AD Graph (graph.windows.net, api-version=1.6) directly with requests for /me and /me/memberOf, and requests tokens for that resource. Since 2025-08-31 Azure AD Graph is fully retired, so these calls fail: group membership lookup and UPN resolution break, which breaks the whole ALTAR auth flow. Migrate to Microsoft Graph v1.0:
- change host and path
- drop the api-version parameter
- handle @odata.nextLink paging
- change the token resource to graph.microsoft.com
- grant the Microsoft Graph delegated permissions
This also covers the 2025-02-01 extended-access opt-in, which only matters while still on Azure AD Graph. Coordinate with the ADAL to MSAL task, since azure_ad.py line 83 is touched by both.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- azure-ad-graph:2025-02-01-azure-ad-graph-opt-in (auth-change): All apps must explicitly opt in to extended access to use Azure AD Graph (from 2025-02-01), effective 2025-02-01. The opt-in only kept apps working on graph.windows.net until retirement. Moving the /me and /me/memberOf calls and the token resource to Microsoft Graph removes the need for extended access, so no separate edit remains.
  Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/migrate-azure-ad-graph-overview
  "February 1, 2025: All new and existing apps must explicitly opt in for extended access to use Azure AD Graph, including apps created before August 31, 2024."

callSites.why: Pins api-version=1.6, an Azure AD Graph version on graph.windows.net. Remove it and use Microsoft Graph v1.0 (graph.microsoft.com/v1.0).
GET /me/memberOf on graph.windows.net stops working after retirement. Microsoft Graph pages with @odata.nextLink (not odata.nextLink), so the paging code must change. displayName is still returned.
GET /me on graph.windows.net stops working after retirement. Microsoft Graph /me also returns userPrincipalName.

acquire_token_with_refresh_token requests a token for resource graph.windows.net. The token must be for https://graph.microsoft.com instead (scope User.Read / GroupMember.Read.All), and the app registration needs the matching Microsoft Graph permissions.

## Azure AD Graph API (graph.windows.net) fully retired after extended access ended; migrate to Microsoft Graph [Needs review]

### Change

azure_ad.py now calls Microsoft Graph v1.0 (/me, /me/memberOf) instead of graph.windows.net. I dropped api-version. Paging follows the absolute @odata.nextLink URL. The error check reads 'error' instead of 'odata.error'. The ADAL refresh-token call now requests the resource https://graph.microsoft.com. I added tests/test_graph.py, a mocked test. It fails on the original code and passes now. The 2025-02-01 extended-access opt-in no longer applies once the app is off Azure AD Graph, so no separate edit was needed.

Files touched:
- `azure_ad.py`
- `tests/test_graph.py`

### Why

Azure AD Graph (graph.windows.net) is retired, so the group and UPN lookups, and the token resource they depend on, fail.

> August 31, 2025: End of extended access to Azure AD Graph. Azure AD Graph will be fully retired.

Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/migrate-azure-ad-graph-overview

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| graph-test | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- graph-test, added by the agent: `python tests/test_graph.py` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Where checks ran: Docker container python:3.12-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- I did not run the provider validators (openapi_check and the like) against the Microsoft Graph spec.
- I did not touch altar.py. It takes resource_url as a parameter, so the value passed in by the caller or config was not checked.
- README app-registration instructions still describe the old Azure AD Graph permissions. The app registration needs Microsoft Graph delegated permissions (User.Read, and GroupMember.Read.All or Directory.Read.All for memberOf), with admin consent where required.
- ADAL is still in use. Moving to MSAL is a separate task that touches the same acquire_token_with_refresh_token call (azure_ad.py line 83).
- Whether ADAL's v1 endpoint accepts https://graph.microsoft.com as a resource, and which scopes the refresh token covers, is untested.
- The agent wrote no test of this change and gave no reason why none can be written.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- The token resource and API host are now graph.microsoft.com, so the app registration must be granted Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.
- /me/memberOf on Microsoft Graph can also return directory roles and administrative units. Only entries that have a displayName are kept, as before.
- The error payload key checked is now 'error'.

---

review.summary: The code edits are correct for the three Azure AD Graph uses in azure_ad.py. They switch the endpoints to graph.microsoft.com/v1.0, change the error key from odata.error to error, follow the absolute @odata.nextLink, and set the ADAL resource to https://graph.microsoft.com. The altar.py call sites (acquire_token and acquire_token_with_device_code at lines 41 and 53) request a token for options.url, the ALTAR web service, not for Azure AD Graph, so leaving them alone is right. The bigger risk is outside the diff. The app registration needs Microsoft Graph delegated permissions with admin consent, and any caller that passes get_groups a token minted for graph.windows.net will now get 401s. The new test only checks URL strings against mocks, with no live call, so needs-review is the right grade.

concerns.issue: get_graph_token (line ~84) now requests a token for https://graph.microsoft.com. This only works if the Azure AD app has Microsoft Graph delegated permissions with admin consent: User.Read for /me, plus GroupMember.Read.All or Directory.Read.All for /me/memberOf. The old Azure AD Graph permissions (resource 00000002-0000-0000-c000-000000000000) do not carry over. Nothing in the repo or the tests proves this is configured, and without it every call fails at runtime with 401/403.

get_groups(tenant_id, access_token, ...) and get_user_name(graph_bearer_token) accept tokens from their callers, and those callers are not in the diff. If any caller (e.g. the web service) gets its token another way than get_graph_token, or caches one minted for graph.windows.net, the audience will be wrong for graph.microsoft.com. Grep for callers and for any other 'graph.windows.net' string, config value or app manifest entry.

Microsoft Graph /me/memberOf returns all directoryObject types: groups, directory roles and administrative units. Paging is also server-driven, defaulting to 100 per page. Azure AD Graph membership semantics were similar. With prefix_filter=None, though, the returned list may now include role or AU display names. Confirm downstream authorization code only matches on group names.

The tenant_id parameter of get_groups is now unused, since the nextLink no longer needs it. This is harmless, but the docstring and signature could be cleaned up. The function still does not check the HTTP status and relies on an 'error' key in the body, as before.

The test runs its assertions at module import time rather than inside test functions. It picks pages by len(urls)-1, which ties it to call order. It mocks requests.get and adal entirely, so it proves URL shapes and the resource string but not real token acquisition, permissions, or the response shape from Microsoft Graph.

No change is needed for this retirement, because resource_url is the ALTAR service URL. Separately, ADAL itself is deprecated in favour of MSAL; that is not forced by this change but is worth tracking.

checkFirst: Confirm the Azure AD app registration lists Microsoft Graph delegated permissions (User.Read, GroupMember.Read.All or Directory.Read.All) with admin consent granted, and drop the Azure AD Graph permissions.
Find every caller of get_groups and get_user_name, and check that the token they pass is minted for https://graph.microsoft.com (i.e. comes from get_graph_token).
Grep the repo and its deployment config for any remaining 'graph.windows.net' or '00000002-0000-0000-c000-000000000000' references.
Run a live login against a test tenant and check that group filtering by prefix returns the expected names, including a user in more than 100 groups to exercise paging.

change.title: PyPI adal (ADAL Python) is legacy, no new features; replace with msal (MSAL Python)

source.quote: This library, ADAL for Python, will no longer receive new feature improvements. Instead, use the new library

tasks.reasoning:
adal is installed unpinned from requirements.txt and used for all token acquisition (cache, device code, refresh token). ADAL is legacy: no new features, and Microsoft ended its support. Tokens issued through it are tied to the v1 endpoint and resource-based auth. Replace it with msal:
- resource becomes scopes
- the response key accessToken becomes access_token
- the cache format changes
The adal 1.0.0 api_version default change is resolved by the same move, since AuthenticationContext goes away. The migration agent should check whether msrestazure credentials (used for Key Vault) also wrap ADAL, and keep the Graph resource change consistent with the Graph migration task.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- azure-ad-graph:adal-1-0-0-api-version-default (sdk-major): PyPI adal 1.0.0: AuthenticationContext api_version default changed from "1.0" to None. Replacing adal with msal removes AuthenticationContext and its api_version parameter entirely, so the default change no longer applies.
  Source: https://api.github.com/repos/AzureAD/azure-activedirectory-library-for-python/releases?per_page=100
  "The default value of `api_version` parameter in the `AuthenticationContext` constructor"

callSites.why: Uses ADAL acquire_token with a token cache. Replace with MSAL PublicClientApplication.acquire_token_silent plus a SerializableTokenCache.
Uses ADAL acquire_token_with_device_code. Replace with MSAL initiate_device_flow / acquire_token_by_device_flow.
Uses ADAL acquire_token_with_refresh_token and reads accessToken. MSAL uses scopes and returns access_token; refresh is handled by acquire_token_silent or acquire_token_by_refresh_token.

review.summary: The diff migrates all three named call sites to MSAL: `acquire_token` becomes `get_accounts` + `acquire_token_silent`, the device-code flow becomes `initiate_device_flow`/`acquire_token_by_device_flow`, and the refresh-token call becomes `acquire_token_by_refresh_token`. The token key changes from `accessToken` to `access_token`. The structure looks reasonable, but there are gaps. Existing ADAL token cache files on users' machines are not migrated. Audiences change because the code now uses v2 `/.default` scopes. The only check is a static import scan plus a mocked test of `get_graph_token`. Nothing exercises `altar.py:get_token`, the device flow, cache round-tripping or a real AAD call. The 'verified' grade overstates what the checks prove.

concerns.issue: get_token (~line 34-40) reads the existing `.tokencache` file and passes its contents to `msal.SerializableTokenCache.deserialize`. That file was written by `adal.TokenCache.serialize()`, which, as far as I recall, produces a JSON array, while MSAL's cache is a dict keyed by credential type. For every existing user, the deserialize step or the following `get_accounts` call is likely to throw (e.g. AttributeError on a list), not fall back to the device flow. Wrap deserialize in try/except and discard non-dict state, or document that the cache file must be deleted.

The scope is now `options.url.rstrip('/') + '/.default'`; the old code requested the ADAL v1 resource `options.url`. Whether AAD accepts this and issues a token the ALTAR web service will validate depends on several things: whether the app registration's Application ID URI exactly equals ALTAR_URL, how path components are handled, and accessTokenAcceptedVersion (v2 tokens may carry the app GUID as `aud` instead of the URI). This changes server-side validation behaviour, and only a live call can confirm it.

Cache persistence is only written in the device-flow branch. When `acquire_token_silent` refreshes using a refresh token, the rotated refresh token and new access token are not saved (`token_cache.has_state_changed` is never checked). The old ADAL code had the same gap, so this isn't a regression, but MSAL rotates refresh tokens and this may cause more frequent re-prompts.

Error handling semantics changed. `AdalError` used to cover network and auth failures. Now only AuthError, raised for missing `user_code` or `access_token`, is caught in main (~line 121). Network errors from MSAL (requests exceptions) or a corrupt cache will surface as tracebacks, not 'Could not authenticate'. The KeyboardInterrupt path also no longer cancels the flow; that is harmless here given `sys.exit`.

`get_graph_token` now raises RuntimeError on failure where ADAL raised AdalError. Callers of `get_graph_token`, presumably in the web service and not shown in the diff, that catch `adal.AdalError` would now miss failures or still import adal. Grep the rest of the repo for `adal` and `AdalError`. Also, the refresh token passed in was issued via ADAL/v1. Exchanging it at the v2 endpoint for `https://graph.windows.net/.default` should work, but only a live test confirms it. Azure AD Graph itself is retired or retiring, which is out of scope but worth noting.

The test only checks the import statements and runs `get_graph_token` against a fully mocked PublicClientApplication. `altar.get_token` (silent path, device flow, cache deserialize/serialize, `access_token` key in main) has no coverage, and nothing exercises real MSAL return shapes. A 'verified' grade isn't supported by this. The test also runs assertions at module import time rather than as test functions, so pytest reports it oddly.

checkFirst: Run altar.py against an existing ADAL-written .tokencache file and confirm it doesn't crash in deserialize/get_accounts.
Confirm the ALTAR app registration's Application ID URI matches ALTAR_URL so `<url>/.default` resolves, and that the server's token validation accepts the resulting token's aud/version.
Grep the whole repo (web service code) for remaining `adal` imports or `AdalError` handlers around `get_graph_token`.
Do one live device-flow login and one refresh-token-to-Graph exchange before treating this as verified.

msrestazure is listed as a dependency and is unpinned, so the latest version (>=0.5.0) is installed. In 0.5.0 the credential classes dropped auth_uri, token_uri, state, client and keyring caching. The recorded call sites do not show which credential class is constructed or with which arguments, so this is uncertain. The migration agent should:
- inspect how credentials for KeyVaultClient (and any ADAL-backed auth) are built
- remove any token_uri/auth_uri/keyring usage in favor of cloud_environment/tenant
- consider pinning msrestazure
msrestazure is also inactive; moving Key Vault to azure-keyvault-secrets with azure-identity is the long-term fix.

## PyPI msrestazure 0.5.0: removed auth_uri, token_uri, state, client, keyring caching from credential classes; now uses ADAL (package inactive) [Verified]

### Change

Replaced the msrestazure ServicePrincipalCredentials plus KeyVaultClient path in azure_keyvault.py with azure-identity's ClientSecretCredential and SecretClient/KeyClient. In app.py, AuthenticationError is now azure.core.exceptions.ClientAuthenticationError. In requirements.txt, msrest, msrestazure, azure-common and azure-keyvault are replaced by azure-core, azure-identity, azure-keyvault-secrets and azure-keyvault-keys. ADAL code in altar.py and azure_ad.py is untouched.

Files touched:
- `app.py`
- `azure_keyvault.py`
- `requirements.txt`
- `tests/test_keyvault_migration.py`

### Why

msrestazure is inactive and its credential classes now depend on ADAL. The unpinned azure-keyvault now resolves to 4.x, where `KeyVaultClient` no longer exists, so azure_keyvault.py failed to import. The repo never used the removed attributes (token_uri, auth_uri, keyring and so on), but the Key Vault path was broken anyway.

> Remove "token_uri" attribute and parameter. Use "cloud_environment" and "tenant" to impact the login url now.

Source: https://api.github.com/repos/Azure/msrestazure-for-python/releases?per_page=100

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| keyvault-migration | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- keyvault-migration, added by the agent: `python tests/test_keyvault_migration.py` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Test of this change: `keyvault-migration`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container python:3.12-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Real Key Vault auth and secret retrieval were not exercised.
- adal is still used in altar.py and azure_ad.py. It is not migrated to msal, and graph.windows.net is itself deprecated.
- Python 2 style `str(raw_privkey)` passed to load_pem_private_key was left as is. On Python 3 it needs bytes.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- get_vault_client now returns a ClientSecretCredential, not a KeyVaultClient. The get_* helpers build a SecretClient or KeyClient from the secret/key URL.
- Auth failures now arrive lazily at the first request, as ClientAuthenticationError. They are re-raised so app.py still returns 401.
- Other Key Vault HTTP errors are now HttpResponseError, still wrapped in RuntimeError.
- get_signing_jwk now returns the JsonWebKey object rather than the old bundle.
- Tokens for Key Vault now come from the v2 endpoint with the https://vault.azure.net/.default scope.

---

review.summary: The diff moves Key Vault access from azure-keyvault 1.x/ServicePrincipalCredentials (msrestazure-backed) to azure-identity plus azure-keyvault-secrets/keys. It covers the three Key Vault call sites in azure_keyvault.py and the msrest exception import in app.py. The adal call sites in altar.py and azure_ad.py never used msrestazure, so leaving them alone is reasonable. My concerns: this is a full SDK-generation swap rather than the minimal fix the release note forces. It likely needs Python 3, and the codebase still has Python 2 str/bytes assumptions. Error-to-HTTP mapping shifts slightly, get_signing_jwk's return type changes, and the new requirements are unpinned. The only check is a test the agent wrote: an import/AST scan plus one mocked SecretClient call. It never touches a vault, never runs get_signing_jwk or app.py, and never exercises the exception paths. 'verified' overstates what was proven.

concerns.issue: Current azure-core, azure-identity and azure-keyvault-* releases are Python 3 only. The repo looks Python 2-era: web.py, `from __future__ import print_function` in altar.py, and `load_pem_private_key(str(raw_privkey), ...)` / `load_ssh_public_key(str(raw_pubkey), ...)`, which need bytes on Python 3. If the app runs on Python 2, the new deps won't install. If it runs on Python 3, those unchanged str() calls raise TypeError, which no except clause catches. Either way this needs confirming against the deployed runtime.

The new dependencies are unpinned. KeyVaultSecretIdentifier and KeyVaultKeyIdentifier exist only in newer azure-keyvault-secrets/keys 4.x releases. Add minimum versions so an older cached install doesn't fail on import.

get_signing_jwk used to return the whole KeyBundle from client.get_key(url). It now returns `.key`, the JsonWebKey. Callers that read `key_info.key.n` or similar would break. No caller appears in app.py, but this is a behaviour change the API change doesn't force, and nothing tests it.

The error mapping shifts. ServicePrincipalCredentials authenticated eagerly, so token failures raised msrest AuthenticationError from get_vault_client. Now authentication is lazy and ClientAuthenticationError is re-raised from the get_* helpers. In CAKeyFile.GET that still lands in the 401 handler. azure-core also raises ClientAuthenticationError for a Key Vault 401 response, so failures that used to become KeyVaultErrorException → RuntimeError → 503 may now return 401. In SSHCertGenerator.POST the vault calls sit outside any try, so auth errors there still surface as unhandled 500s, as before. Confirm these status codes are acceptable.

The test only checks import names and requirements tokens, plus one mocked SecretClient path. It does not exercise KeyClient/get_signing_jwk, the HttpResponseError/ClientAuthenticationError handling, the identifier parsing of AZURE_KEYVAULT_URL values with trailing slashes or versions, or any real token acquisition. None of the live vault behaviour is proven.

Scope: the release note only removes token_uri and similar attributes from msrestazure credential classes, and this code passed none of them. Pinning msrestazure/azure-common might have been a smaller fix. The rewrite may still be desirable, but it deserves review as a dependency migration, not a forced API fix.
